newsitem.title: UK: Sterling/mark hits 57-mth high as mark stumbles.
newsitem.headline: Sterling/mark hits 57-mth high as mark stumbles.

text.p: Sterling marched to its highest against the mark since August 1992, helped by the German currency's weakness against its European counterparts amid rekindled optimism about Europe's monetary union.

With the currency market focusing on the fate of EMU, which traders and analysts said was looking increasingly like start with a broad-based membership, sterling was benefitting as a safe-haven currency outside the EMU group.

"There's been a lot of noise about EMU, making people nervous about the more solid block of EMU currencies and giving more weight to sterling in the market," said Paul Crowhurst, head of forwards at Bank of Boston in London.
"No-one particularly wants to buy European currencies, perhaps sterling is presenting a good place to put money," Crowhurst said.

The pound briefly touched a high of 2.8360 marks in afternoon trade, although it had subsided to 2.8310/00 by 1343 GMT. However, it was still above the 2.8235/45 level it was at in late European trade on Thursday.

Analysts said sterling/mark was now at a crucial level from the technical viewpoint. If it can stay above 2.8330 -- a former multi-year high touched twice since the beginning of May -- this would herald a further rise, they said.

"If we do make a clear break of this resistance (of 2.8330 marks), we're going to move into a new trading range up towards 2.85," said Tom Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull in London.
"But the UK data next week may be softer, and sterling might drop back again towards 2.80," he said.
The pound was also helped by softer-than-expected economic data out of the U.S. today and yesterday, which dampened dollar sentiment briefly and let the pound take the bulk of the EMU overflow.
U.S. inflation data today showed the producer prices index had dropped 0.3 percent in May against a rise of 0.1 percent. On Thursday, data showed April retail sales dropped 0.1 percent on the month.

"The data today showed no sign of inflationary pressures, and we had the weak retail sales. I think we're looking at the Fed on hold, at least definitely at the next meeting (of the Federal Open Market Committee). So that's helping sterling," SocGen's Rayner said.
Cable was at $1.6365/75, off its session high of $1.6403 but up from its late Thursday level of $1.6345/55.
Against the yen, sterling continued to recover after hitting a seven-month low of 181.31 on Wednesday. It was at its session high of 187.45/73, up from late Thursday's 186.60.
